children: (“NKGen” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative autologous and allogeneic natural killer (“NK”) cell therapeutics, today announced that NKGen Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul Y. Song, M.D., will present on the Company’s lead investigational program, troculeucel, at the 4th Great Bay Cell and Gene Therapy Forum, taking place September 22-23, 2026, in Guangzhou, China.
Autologous Enhanced Natural Killer Cell Therapy for Neurodegenerative Diseases
Next Gen Cell Therapy Track 3 -- Autoimmunity & Universal Cell Therapy
Wednesday, September 23, 2026, at 9:35– 10:00 a.m. China Standard Time (CST)/Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 9:35-10:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET)

Dr. Song’s presentation will explore the application of troculeucel in neurodegenerative diseases, with a focus on its proposed mechanism of action, changes observed in neuroinflammatory and protein biomarkers in cerebrospinal fluid, and clinical experience in patients with Alzheimer’s disease. The presentation will also discuss Parkinson’s disease and frontotemporal dementia as potential areas for further evaluation of troculeucel.

Troculeucel is a novel cell-based, patient specific, ex vivo expanded autologous NK cell immunotherapeutic drug candidate. NKGen is developing troculeucel for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders and a broad range of cancers. Troculeucel is the International Nonproprietary Name (“INN”) for SNK01 assigned by the World Health Organization (“WHO”). The WHO INN approval of troculeucel establishes a universally recognized nonproprietary drug name for SNK01 and marks a significant step on NKGen’s journey toward bringing this therapy to market.

NKGen is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative autologous and allogeneic NK cell therapeutics. NKGen is headquartered in Santa Ana, California, USA. For more information, please visit www.nkgenbiotech.com.
